Research/2025-26/Galactic center

Galactic center

Investigating the Origins of the Fermi Bubbles with CMHD Simulations

A simulation-based comparison of two explanations for the enormous bipolar structures above and below the Milky Way.

Research question

What did the project ask?

Which proposed origin better reproduces the Fermi Bubbles: episodic jets from Sagittarius A* or sustained star-formation-driven Galactic winds?

Significance

Why does it matter?

Distinguishing these models would clarify the recent energetic history of the Galactic Center.

Method

What did the team do?

The team used the PLUTO computational magnetohydrodynamics code to model an active-galactic-nucleus jet scenario and a Galactic-wind scenario, then compared their large-scale morphologies with the observed bubble structure.

Principal result

What did the evidence show?

Both models generated bipolar outflows. The jet model produced sharper, vertically directed lobes that the poster judged more consistent with Fermi-LAT morphology than the broader radial outflow from the Galactic-wind model. This was a morphological comparison, not a quantitative fit across observatories.
